When target behavior is version-sensitive, does missing exact target source remain EVIDENCE_REQUIRED rather than being closed by a newer-version analog?
For every replicated reference relation/value, is the authoritative owner named and is semantic validity distinguished from mere existence/type validity?
Is freshness observable through a timestamp/version/hash/export batch or another reproducible fingerprint instead of assumed from a successful previous sync?
Is the propagation chain traced end-to-end (authoritative source → exchange/export → server/base/cache → device/client consumer) with each independently stale boundary identified?

When observed behavior can be explained by stale replicated data, is a controlled refresh/re-export/reload diagnostic performed before modifying business code, while preserving evidence of the before/after state?
Can an existing but semantically incorrect mapping/reference be rejected or surfaced, rather than accepted merely because the record/reference is technically valid?
Does runtime acceptance cover current-data success and, where material, stale/invalid-data behavior plus propagation after source change?
Could stale or not-yet-propagated reference data be diagnosed as a code defect without first proving current source and downstream snapshots?
Can a technically valid reference/row be accepted as semantically correct without proving the business relation it represents?
Can source master data change while one downstream server/device/cache copy remains stale with no observable propagation contract?
Are raw scanner/input bytes or code points observed before parsing, including non-printable separators such as GS, rather than inferred from a displayed/logged string?
Is there exactly one named normalization owner, with every replacement/trim/escape/encoding transformation justified and testable before classification?
When multiple templates/classifiers can match the same prefix, is specificity/precedence explicit so a broad fallback cannot steal a more specific valid code?
Are full, shortened, transport and scanner-specific representations treated as equivalent only when the domain/parser contract explicitly proves that equivalence and information loss is acceptable?
Are trade-item GTIN, individual serial/mark, logistics SSCC/container and regulatory aggregation identities classified by domain role before business routing?
Does runtime acceptance distinguish emulator/manual paste from the actual scanner/device/keyboard-wedge path when control characters or encoding can differ?
When parsing fails, can diagnostics identify the raw/normalized/classified stage and competing matched pattern without exposing sensitive payload more broadly than necessary?
Can printable text such as '0029' or an escaped display representation be treated as the actual GS control character without byte/code-point evidence?
Can a broad prefix-only barcode pattern win before a more specific KM/GS1/SSCC classifier and silently change business routing?
Can a shortened/normalized code be treated as semantically identical to the full scanned code without proving which AI/data fields were removed and whether downstream validation needs them?
Can successful emulator/manual-input parsing be used as proof of physical scanner behavior when separators, prefix/suffix handling or encoding may differ?
Is the mode represented as an explicit finite set of states/transitions (or an equivalent proven contract) rather than independent flags whose combinations can become invalid?
Is one owner named for mode state, selected row/object and transient input, with lifetime scoped to the correct form/session/scenario?
Are enter → consume/success → reset transitions explicit, including which business action consumes the temporary mode?
Do cancel, invalid input, no-data/empty-result, exception and user-abort paths reset or preserve state according to an explicit contract rather than only the happy path?
When selection/current row/object changes, is stale mode-bound data invalidated or rebound deliberately before the next action?
Are repeated command/re-entry semantics explicit so a second activation cannot stack, invert or reuse stale transient state accidentally?
Do form close/reopen and navigation away/back clear or restore only intentional state, with acceptance proving the next ordinary action is unaffected?
Can temporary UI mode be reset only after successful completion while error/cancel/no-data paths leave it armed for the next unrelated action?
Can the selected/current row change while a temporary mode still carries data or assumptions from the previous row?
Can close/reopen or repeated command entry consume transient state created by a previous attempt instead of starting from the documented initial state?
Is the business identity/projection that must exist immediately before the external side effect explicitly defined and validated?
Is the exact identity/data projection sent to or irreversibly observed by the external system proven independently from the object's later internal state?
Is there an exact success/acknowledgement boundary after which post-success internal identity transformation is allowed, rather than treating call initiation as success?
Can post-success mutation occur only after confirmed external success, with failure/exception paths leaving the retry identity and payload contract intact?

On retry/re-entry, is it explicit whether the original external payload identity or transformed internal identity must be reused, and is idempotency/correlation sufficient to prevent duplicate or inconsistent external effects?
Are downstream documents/reports/registers deliberately bound to the intended pre- or post-side-effect identity instead of assuming they are still the same?
When a reverse/refund/cancel pipeline exists, is its identity source and external/internal ordering independently traced and accepted rather than copied by analogy from the forward flow?
Is there an auditable correlation from the external receipt/message/result to the internal object before and after identity transformation so discrepancies can be reconstructed?
Can identity mutation after an external success be reviewed as an ordinary local write without proving what the external system already observed and the exact temporal boundary?
After external failure or ambiguous completion, can a retry accidentally use the post-mutation identity/payload even though the external contract expects the original pre-side-effect projection?
Can the external payload and later internal identity intentionally diverge without an explicit correlation/audit contract proving both representations belong to the same business event?
Is the derived decision/classification named together with every material dependency that can change its truth value?
For every mutable dependency, is the authoritative current value/source named rather than relying on a stale UI/cache snapshot?
Does every dependency change have an explicit invalidation/revalidation policy, including whether existing rows/results are rechecked immediately, lazily before use, or intentionally left unchanged?
Before a previously computed decision is consumed after context change/re-entry, is freshness proven or revalidation executed at a deterministic boundary?

Can cached/row-level validation state survive a counterparty, agreement, organization, warehouse, discount-card, role, date/status or other material context change without proof that the decision remains valid?
Runtime acceptance covers a decision before and after changing at least one material dependency, including the expected treatment of already existing rows/results.
Can the system reuse a decision that was valid under context A after a dependency changes to context B, without invalidation or revalidation?
For each material source→target business relation, is allowed cardinality explicitly stated as zero/one/many on both directions where relevant?
If implementation selects the first/only related object, is uniqueness proven by metadata/business invariant or is ambiguity handled explicitly instead of inferred from current data?
Are zero, exactly one and multiple related-object outcomes each assigned deterministic behavior: continue, aggregate, split, choose by an explicit rule, or block?
When several source objects may contribute to one target (or one source to several targets), are merge/split identity and duplication rules explicit?
Acceptance covers representative 0/1/N relation cases rather than only the singleton case present in one test database.
Can ВЫБРАТЬ ПЕРВЫЕ 1/first-found logic silently convert a potentially 1:N business relation into 1:1 without a proven uniqueness contract?
Is a 1:1 relation being inferred only because current sample/test data happened to contain one related object?
Is the conserved business fact/measure named separately from the allocation dimension being changed (box/container/series/project/warehouse/other analytic)?
Does the operation mutate allocation ownership without accidentally changing the total fact unless the business operation explicitly adds/removes fact?
Is a conservation invariant explicit (for example Σ fact before = Σ fact after) with identity/quantity normalization defined?
If an intermediate UNASSIGNED/unallocated state is allowed, are its owner, lifetime and permitted next transitions explicit?
Does completion block when required fact remains unallocated, duplicated or over-allocated?
Are repeated move/re-entry/retry operations idempotent with respect to total fact and allocation identity?
Runtime acceptance proves conservation across move A→B, temporary unassignment when allowed, repeated move and final completion.
Can reassigning an existing fact between analytics/containers increase or decrease total fact even though the business action only changes allocation?
Can a document/process complete while conserved fact remains in a temporary unassigned state that the business contract requires to be fully allocated?

blocking_rule: Every activated profile/rule requires evidence-backed disposition; generated views cannot silently add/remove rules.
reverse_coverage_rule: Expand checks from RULES/rule_registry.json independently from code-driven findings.
